teaching_card.title: Coordinate Geometry (Medium)
teaching_card.body: Points in the (x, y) plane are connected by three formulas: the distance formula (a hidden Pythagorean theorem), the midpoint formula (average the coordinates), and the slope. A circle with center (h, k) and radius r is (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r².
key_points: Parallel lines share a slope; perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals.
Circle: (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r², center (h, k).

screens.title: Distance and midpoint
screens.body: Draw the right triangle between two points: the legs are the differences in x and y, and the distance is the hypotenuse. The midpoint is simply the average of the x's and the average of the y's. If a midpoint and one endpoint are known, double the midpoint and subtract the endpoint.
key_points: Distance: square the differences, add, take the root.
Midpoint: add and halve each coordinate.

screens.title: Lines: parallel and perpendicular
screens.body: Rewrite Ax + By = C as y = (−A/B)x + C/B to read the slope. A parallel line keeps that slope; a perpendicular line uses the negative reciprocal (flip the fraction and change the sign). Then use the given point to find the intercept with y = mx + b.
key_points: Slope of Ax + By = C is −A/B.
A point is on a line if it satisfies the equation.

screens.title: Circles in the plane
screens.body: In (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r², the signs inside the parentheses are opposite to the center's coordinates, and the right side is r², not r. For an expanded equation x² + y² + Dx + Ey + F = 0, complete the square: the center is (−D/2, −E/2).
key_points: Complete the square to recover the center.

screens.title: Try the moves
screens.body: Line through (2, 1) perpendicular to y = 2x + 5: slope −1/2, so 1 = −1/2·2 + b gives b = 2 and y = −x/2 + 2. Circle x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 3 = 0: (x − 2)² + (y + 3)² = 16, center (2, −3), radius 4.
